subject: Request: One-time onboarding subsidy & temporary pilot price floor for BrightLeaf — exec signoff
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Grant <ethan@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: One-time onboarding subsidy & temporary pilot price floor for BrightLeaf — exec signoff

Ethan / BrightLeaf team —

Thanks again for a great demo last week. Per our conversation, BrightLeaf is ready to run a 90-day pilot across two product streams (ingest + inference) with expected peak concurrent queries around 60 rps and an initial estimated token volume of ~45M tokens / month. This pilot is strategic for us given their roadmap and the potential to scale into a multi-year enterprise account.

Ask: we are requesting approval to offer a one-time onboarding subsidy and a temporary pilot price floor to remove early friction on adoption. Proposed terms: 
- One-time onboarding subsidy: $25,000 credit applied against first two monthly invoices (to cover integration work and initial training).
- Temporary pilot price floor: 30% discount off list (applied for the 90-day pilot period, capped at $30k total discount).

Rationale: BrightLeaf has explicit multi-product expansion signals, a procurement timeline that pushes production into Q4, and references that accelerate our go-to-market in the healthcare vertical. The subsidy buys seat/time for our solutions engineers and offsets their initial integration costs.

Attachments: BL-pilot-MAP.xlsx (mutual action plan), price-models.xlsx (sensitivity to usage).

Requested approvals / next steps:
1) Marissa — business approval to proceed with a one-time subsidy & pilot discount.
2) Ben — CFO signoff for subsidy cap and accounting treatment (revenue recognition & crediting).
3) Grace — confirm SOW timeline & any operational constraints.

If approved, I'll send a short amendment and the draft SOW to BrightLeaf today and request a signature.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

--
Attachment stubs: BL-pilot-MAP.xlsx (spreadsheet), price-models.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Ethan Grant <ethan@brightleaf.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 09:45:31 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: One-time onboarding subsidy & temporary pilot price floor for BrightLeaf — exec signoff

Jordan — thanks for the quick turnaround. The terms look reasonable from our side. A few clarifications so procurement can move fast: 
- Does the subsidy require any milestone delivery or is it an unconditional credit?
- Can we get a short SLA commitment for the pilot (99.5% for inference path) and a support contact for escalation?
- For the discount cap, can you confirm whether egress/storage costs are excluded (we'll likely incur some egress during exports)?

If we can get answers today, I can get internal approvals and sign the SOW by Friday.

—Ethan
Ethan Grant
Head of Platform Partnerships, BrightLeaf Analytics
ethan@brightleaf.ai

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: One-time onboarding subsidy & temporary pilot price floor for BrightLeaf — exec signoff

Ethan — quick answers inline: 
- Subsidy: one-time credit applied to invoices; no usage-milestone gating. We ask for a 30-day review to ensure integration progress but credits are applied up-front to mitigate ops friction.
- SLA: we will provide a 99.5% availability commitment for the inference endpoints for the pilot; escalation path will be Grace O'Connor (solutions lead) + SOC on-call. I'll add SLA language to the draft SOW.
- Egress/storage: excluded from the discount and billed per standard list; we will call out egress explicitly in the amendment so there's no surprise on cap calculations.

I've uploaded BrightLeaf-SOW-draft.pdf to the Drive link and attached the revised MAP (minor timeline tweak). If Marissa and Ben can approve the subsidy & cap as outlined (credit = $25k; discount = 30% capped at $30k), I'll issue the amendment and request signature today.

Jordan

--
Attachment stub: BrightLeaf-SOW-draft.pdf (PDF)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: One-time onboarding subsidy & temporary pilot price floor for BrightLeaf — exec signoff

Jordan — thanks for the clear memo. I support the commercial rationale for a limited subsidy here given the potential expansion and references. A couple of notes before CFO sign-off: 
- Please draft a short one-page justification memo that states expected ARR progression (conservative + upside) and calls out reference customers and product overlap. Attach that to the amendment.
- Finance (Ben) will need a note on revenue recognition impact and whether the credit is treated as a contra-revenue or deferred inducement.

I've uploaded an approval-justification-memo.pdf with my business rationale and recommended cap. Please route this to Ben directly with the draft amendment.

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 May 2028 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: One-time onboarding subsidy & temporary pilot price floor for BrightLeaf — exec signoff

Team — after reviewing the materials and Marissa's memo, CFO conditional approval granted with the following guardrails: 
1) Subsidy cap set to $25,000 (applied as credit across the first two invoices).
2) Discount floor allowed at up to 30% for the 90-day pilot, but total vendor impact capped at $30,000. Any delta beyond $30k requires VP-level re-approval.
3) Require prepayment of the first month of expected invoice (or a signed PO committing to the pilot spend) to mitigate bad-debt risk.
4) Finance will treat the subsidy as a contra-revenue credit and will record a 90-day monitoring reversal if the account churns before Q4 conversion; accounting will flag this in the forecast.
5) Schedule a 90-day commercial review (Jordan + Grace + Marissa + Finance) to evaluate performance and decide on conversion pricing.

Jordan — you have my go-ahead to issue the amendment with the above conditions. Please include the approval-justification-memo.pdf and the BrightLeaf-SOW-draft.pdf in the signature packet and confirm prepayment/PO with Ethan before routing to legal for a narrow amendment.

Ben Carter
CFO, Redwood Inference
